Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity evaluation + throughput baseline

Hi Rachel,

We self-signed up via the Redwood docs and would like a walkthrough focused on dedicated capacity sizing. High-level requirements below:

- Workload: synchronous text-generation API for search-ranking enrichment
- Target sustained throughput: 450–600 QPS (avg payload ~32 tokens)
- Latency target: p95 < 180ms for generation path (end-to-end)
- Typical sequences: 16–64 tokens; spike patterns during batch jobs midday

We have a short PDF with example traces attached (Blueforge_Requirements_v2.pdf). Ideally the session covers: slot sizing guidance, batching/caching best practices for steady QPS, and what a production load test looks like on Redwood Dedicated.

Preferred times (ET):
- Tue Nov 9, 11:00–11:45 ET
- Wed Nov 10, 09:00–09:45 ET

If you can’t do those, please propose alternatives. We’d like to include one engineer (ops+infra@blueforge.com).

Cheers,
Samir Patel
Director of ML Ops
Blueforge Labs

--

A couple of clarifications so Ben can size things appropriately:
- Burst behavior: we see short spikes up to ~900 QPS for 2–5 minutes during hourly batch windows
- Warm cache expected for most latencies; cold-starts for new keys not common but possible
- Models: we plan to run a 3B quantized model; we’ll want guidance on kernel/quantization tradeoffs and cost/latency impact

I attached a small CSV with a 24-hour sample of request timestamps (prod_qps_sample.csv). We’re especially interested in what steady-state slot count + burst buffer you’d recommend and any recommended autoscale policy values.
